brief: WEB-728 (R2L-1, S2) is a regression of WP44, found by the L verifier (`verify-b4-r2-L.md`, ‘Regressions’). WP44's five findings came back fixed: keep everything it did (the 52ch body column, the 1rem values, the hidden h2 on phones, the language switch under the request box, the 360 px block, the shorter version line, the copy fixes).

What happens today: on /delete-account/, /es/delete-account/ and /ca/delete-account/ at 320 × 568, light and dark, the request box's ‘Send to’ / «Destinatario» / «Destinatari» value breaks inside the domain: ‘taskflow.support@garbar.t’ over ‘ech’ (renders `delete-account.{en,ca}.mobile-w320.light.full.png`, screen 2). WP44 raised `.legal-mail-details dd` from 0.875rem to 1rem (WEB-205), so the 28-character address is about 234 px wide against about 214 px of room, and `.legal-mail-details`' `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (`legal.css:113`) splits it wherever it runs out. A leaver whose mail app didn't open, copying the address by hand, reads ‘garbar.t’ and ‘ech’.

Fix, from the reviewer: give the address a sensible break point instead of shrinking it. In `LegalPage.tsx:84`, render the recipient value split at the ‘@’ with a `<wbr />` before it, so a narrow box wraps it as ‘taskflow.support’ over ‘@garbar.tech’ and a wide one keeps it on one line. Split the value of `company.contactEmail` (don't hard-code the address), for example `const at = company.contactEmail.indexOf("@");` and `<dd>{at > 0 ? (<>{company.contactEmail.slice(0, at)}<wbr />{company.contactEmail.slice(at)}</>) : company.contactEmail}</dd>`. `<wbr>` adds no character, so the dd's text, a selection and a copy stay exactly `taskflow.support@garbar.tech`; `tests/legal.spec.ts:109` (`toContainText(mail.pathname)`) keeps passing.

Keep `.legal-mail-details dd` at `1rem` (WEB-205's acceptance needs it) and keep `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.legal-mail-details`: it stays the last resort for the subject line and for very large text. No CSS change.

WEB-205 and WEB-204 are listed only so the tester and the L verifier re-check them next to this change; both came back fixed in round 2. Change nothing for them. The email button sits above the mail details, so a taller ‘Send to’ value can't push it down; confirm the existing WEB-204 test still passes.

Test (held), in `tests/ux-web-legal.spec.ts` next to the WEB-205 tests: ‘WEB-728: on the delete pages the support address wraps only at the @’. For /delete-account/, /es/delete-account/ and /ca/delete-account/, light and dark: read the address from the request box's `a.button` `mailto:` href (its pathname); take the first `.legal-mail-details dd`; assert that its `textContent` and, after selecting its contents, `window.getSelection().toString()` both equal that address; then group the dd's characters into rendered lines with one `Range` per character (`getClientRects()`, grouped by top). At 320 × 568 there are one or two lines, and with two they are exactly `taskflow.support` and `@garbar.tech`; at 390 × 664 and 1440 × 1000 there is one line. Use `page.setViewportSize` for 320 × 568, as the WEB-204 test does. Edit with exact-match replacements that keep the file's LF line endings.

Don't touch: `src/styles/legal.css`, the company card's mailto links on /legal/ (`LegalPage.tsx:36`; the verifier found they fit at 320 px), the plain address on the privacy and withdrawal contacts (`LegalPage.tsx:93`, 0.875rem, fits), the subject line, any copy, `src/content/legal/`, the header, the footer, and any file outside `files`.
